title: Invocation Cost Apportioner — Playbook & Prototype
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design a lightweight playbook and interactive prototype for apportioning invocation-level token spend across org entities (teams, projects, seats). Goal: give finance/platform teams a predictable, explainable UI to create republishable allocation recipes, preview effects on historical spend, and export chargeback-ready CSVs. Must integrate with Console rollouts so admins can ship presets tenant-wide and support canary testing for pricing policies.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive allocation editor where admin can assign fixed percentages, rule-based splits (by route, model, or tag), or seat-weighted allocations
History preview shows recalculated monthly spend for selected window (last 30/90/365 days) with delta visualization and sparklines
Export generates CSV with mappings: invocation_id, timestamp, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, unit_cost, allocated_share, charge_code — matches finance schema v1
Presets can be saved and published to org with versioning and A/B rollout flag to test against a control allocation
Latency: preview recalculation for 90d sample under 3s for up to 10M invocations (server-side sampling fallback)
decisions: Use percentage + rule engine hybrid: default to percentage UI, allow adding rules (route/model/tag/seat-weight) that override percentage for matching invocations
Preview will operate on sampled historical data for >1M invocations to keep UI responsive; admin can request a full batch recalculation as a background job
Export schema will align with finance schema v1; any schema changes must be backward compatible and driven by a migration flag
Presets are versioned and visible in Rollouts as a new 'pricing preset' resource to enable canary/A-B testing
tradeoffs: Accuracy vs interactivity: sampling reduces preview precision but enables interactive exploration; full-accuracy runs are background tasks
UI complexity vs discoverability: hiding advanced rule options by default reduces cognitive load but may obscure powerful workflows for power users
Storage & retention: storing per-invocation allocation deltas increases DB size; chosen approach is to persist only the applied preset version and compute allocations on-demand for exports
tasks: Finalize visual language for allocation sliders and rule badges (Design)
Wire up preview API contract with Billing Engs (Eng)
Implement CSV exporter and map fields to finance schema (Billing)
Create rollouts integration spec and versioning model (Platform)
Run 6 moderated usability sessions and synthesize findings (Design Research)
Prepare release notes and admin docs for finance teams (Docs/GA)
Accessibility pass: keyboard + screen reader support for editor controls
ui_notes: Primary editor uses horizontal sliders for percent allocation with numeric input fallback; hovering shows exact token counts recalculated from selected window
Rules expressed as compact chips: if (route matches) then allocate X%; chips can be reordered to indicate priority
History preview panel shows stacked area chart by allocation target with ability to toggle individual streams
Export modal allows selecting time window, currency conversion (USD/EUR), and charge_code mapping table
Save-as-preset modal requires description, intended audience, and 'risk level' tag (low/medium/high) for Rollouts
export_spec: Columns: invocation_id, timestamp, project_id, team_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, unit_cost_usd, allocated_share_percent, allocated_cost_usd, charge_code
Rounding: allocated_cost_usd rounded to 4 decimals; sum of allocated_cost may be adjusted by distributing remainder to smallest allocation to preserve total
Max rows per export: 5M; if >5M, export is chunked and user is notified with links
Audit metadata: export includes header section with preset_id, requestor, generated_at, sampling_note
